terms.gloss: so help me God; as I hope for heaven’s love
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 597: neque, ita mē dī ament, crēdēbam prīmō mihimet Sōsiae
Ter. And. 947: Ita mē dī ament, crēdō.
terms.comment: “So may the gods love me”: an oath that what one says is true (Lewis & Short s.v. amō). Often followed by ut and the thing sworn to.

evidence: Plaut. Aul. 496: Ita mē dī amābunt ut ego hunc auscultō lubēns.

phrases.latin: Ita mē dī amābunt ut ego hunc auscultō lubēns.
phrases.english: So help me God, I do enjoy listening to this man.

phrases.latin: neque, ita mē dī ament, crēdēbam prīmō mihimet Sōsiae
phrases.english: and, so help me God, at first I, Sosia, did not believe my own self

sources: Lewis & Short: amo
